title: Factual Recall: The Capital of France
description: Low entropy factual query where truth has overwhelming probability.
explanation: In factual questions with a single unambiguous answer, the output distribution has extremely low entropy. 'Paris' dominates with a massive logit score. Setting temperature low (e.g., T=0.1) or using Greedy Search yields reliable precision, whereas high temperature (T > 1.5) causes factual hallucination (e.g., 'Lyon' or 'London').

title: Creative Storytelling: The Enchanted Forest
prompt: Deep in the enchanted forest, the ancient wizard discovered a
description: High entropy open-ended creative continuation with diverse valid options.
explanation: In creative writing, there is no single 'correct' next word. The probability mass is spread smoothly across magical artifacts, creatures, and mysterious portals. Greedy decoding picks predictable cliches ('glowing orb'), while Nucleus Sampling (top_p = 0.90, T = 0.85) allows creative variety while filtering out incoherent tails.

title: Degenerative Repetition Loop: Chasing Dogs
prompt: The dog chased the cat and then the cat chased the dog and then
description: Demonstrating greedy search loops and how repetition penalty breaks them.
explanation: Transformers without repetition penalties often get trapped in infinite degenerative self-reinforcing loops. Because 'the dog chased the cat and then' appeared in the context, the model assigns maximum probability to 'the dog'. Raising Repetition Penalty (e.g. 1.25 to 1.50) artificially discounts repeated tokens, forcing the model to break the cycle and introduce fresh progression.

title: Code Completion: Binary Search Implementation
description: Strict deterministic code syntax where exact formula tokens are required.
explanation: Programming code generation demands near-deterministic precision. For calculating the middle index, '(low + high) // 2' is universally expected. Any sampling randomness (high temperature) introduces fatal syntax bugs or incorrect array logic. Code models typically run at T <= 0.2 with top_p <= 0.95.

title: Contextual Bimodal Split: The Batter's Swing
prompt: The baseball player stepped up to the plate and swung his
description: Bi-modal distribution with high probability focused on domain equipment.
explanation: When the sentence context provides strong domain constraints ('baseball player', 'plate'), the model eliminates general nouns and concentrates probability on 'bat' (the tool) with secondary candidates describing the swing style ('arms', 'body'). Nucleus sampling (top_p = 0.90) cleanly clips off irrelevant words.
